chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a long hadith: He said, 'Woe to you, O Bashir! Verily, when a believer visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, and performs Ghusl in the Euphrates, then departs, for every step he takes, a Hajj and an 'Umrah, both accepted and purified, and a Ghaazwah (battle/expedition) with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam are written for him.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): Imam al-Husayn, peace be upon him
key_terms.مَبْرُورَاتٍ: Accepted and purified (referring to acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Ghusl in the Euphrates before visiting Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith underscores the unique status of the Euphrates (Al-Furat) as a sacred medium for purification in Shia tradition, linking physical cleansing with spiritual recognition (*ma'rifah*) of Imam al-Husayn. The reward of 'accepted' (*maqbula*) Hajj and 'Umrah implies freedom from minor sins, while equating each step with a expedition (*ghazwah*) alongside a Prophet or Just Imam elevates the Ziyarah to a continuous act of jihad and devotion.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said – as part of a longer Ḥadīth: Woe unto you, O Bashīr! Verily when a believer goes to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) while knowing his rights and performs Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates (River), with every step that he takes, an accepted and purified Hajj and ‘Umrah and (the reward of) fighting (in the way of Allāh) along with one of Allāh’s messengers or with a Just Imam will be registered for him.
